evidence.claim: Manhattan's 2025 10-K says it develops, sells, deploys, services, and maintains software solutions for supply chains, inventory, and omnichannel operations for retailers, wholesalers, manufacturers, logistics providers, and other organizations.

Manhattan's 2025 10-K identifies core omnichannel applications including Order Management, Store Inventory & Fulfillment, POS, Customer Engagement & Service, enterprise-wide inventory availability determination, and order fulfillment optimization.
SPS Commerce's 2024 Form 10-K says its retail network lets companies manage item details, orders, shipments, invoices, and other workflows for any customer and channel.

SPS Commerce's 2024 Form 10-K says its Fulfillment product streamlines supply-chain operations and enables retailers, grocers, distributors, suppliers, manufacturers, and logistics firms to send and receive order data from order to invoice.

Descartes' fiscal 2025 MD&A says growth in services revenue was driven by global trade intelligence, routing, transportation management solutions, GLN business document exchange, subscriptions, and data content.
Descartes disclosed in a 2025 SEC filing that it acquired 3GTMS, a transportation management solutions provider, and Finale, a cloud-based inventory management provider for ecommerce businesses.
Hackett's 2022 annual report describes business transformation and technology consulting capabilities, including strategic sourcing, procurement, IT, and Oracle-related services.

Gartner's 2025 Magic Quadrant for Warehouse Management Systems lists vendors including Manhattan Associates and Tecsys and states WMS vendors are competing to address demands including cost reduction, automation/robotics support, usability, adaptability, and cloud services.

memory_update.text: MANH should remain the reference anchor for omnichannel OMS/WMS/store-fulfillment orchestration, but not the main underfollowed discovery target.

SPSC is the strongest underfollowed candidate in this pass because its retail trading-partner network directly touches orders, shipments, invoices, fulfillment data, and prebuilt customer/channel integrations.
DSGX is a second-order logistics orchestration candidate; verify how much of revenue is retail/ecommerce fulfillment versus broader trade, routing, customs, and logistics compliance.
HCKT is only a speculative implementation-capacity candidate until direct OMS/WMS/TMS, retail, Manhattan/Blue Yonder/Oracle SCM/SAP SCM, or supply-chain execution project evidence is found.

Need a follow-up search for public implementation partners around Manhattan Active, Blue Yonder, Oracle SCM, SAP EWM/TM, Tecsys, and Descartes; the bottleneck may reside in certified integrator capacity rather than software vendors alone.

node: Omnichannel order-management, warehouse-execution, and fulfillment orchestration software
summary: Expanded the universe for the operational-complexity chokepoint in consumer retail fulfillment. The reference anchor is Manhattan Associates because its public filings directly map to warehouse management, order management, store fulfillment, inventory availability, and transportation workflows. The underfollowed lane is more interesting: SPS Commerce sits in retail trading-partner connectivity and EDI/order document flow; Descartes provides logistics network, routing, transportation, ecommerce inventory and warehouse-adjacent software; Hackett is a smaller implementation/transformation-services shadow candidate where the thesis is less proven but potentially tied to the scarce implementation-capacity bottleneck. No trading recommendation is made.
